plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to zero.
Exit all 2x AI/Software and Semiconductor ETFs (METU, MUU, MSFU, PLTU).
Reduce QQQI allocation to 20% to increase cash buffer.
Hold broad index ETFs (SPY, QQQ) for stability.

conservative.read: This plan prioritizes capital preservation by eliminating leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration. Expect a lower target return, around 1.5% per month, with significantly reduced risk of large drawdowns. The focus is on stability and a larger cash buffer.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to low single digits.
Reduce exposure in 2x AI/Software and Semiconductor ETFs.
Add a new, high-scoring tech name (NBIS) for growth.
Maintain a balanced mix of broad index, quality tech, and some leverage.
Keep a moderate cash buffer for flexibility.
Aim for risk-first growth with controlled drawdowns.
balanced.read: This balanced approach aims for risk-first growth, targeting around 2.5% per month. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a high-quality new name. Expect moderate drawdowns, with a focus on managing risk while seeking growth.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) to 6% each.
Boost allocations in 2x AI/Software and Semiconductor ETFs.
Add a top-rated scanner setup (NBIS) for concentrated growth.
Maintain a smaller cash buffer to maximize invested capital.
Utilize wider, strict stops for risk management.
Aim for aggressive growth, accepting higher potential drawdowns.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets significant growth, aiming for around 4% per month, by leaning into leverage and concentration. It increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and high-scoring tech names. Be aware that this strategy significantly raises both potential upside and downside risk, with leveraged ETFs subject to daily decay and amplified losses.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL) and high-beta tech.
Exit broad index ETFs (QQQ, SPY) to reduce growth volatility.
Increase allocation to income-focused ETF (QQQI) to 30%.
Prioritize steady monthly distributions over capital appreciation.
Maintain a cash buffer for stability.
Focus on low drawdown and reliable income generation.
income.read: This income-focused plan aims for steady monthly distributions, targeting around 1% per month. It significantly reduces risk by selling leveraged and high-beta assets, shifting capital towards income-generating ETFs like QQQI. While prioritizing stability and income, NAV can still decline in market downturns.
